title: Private install observability parity gaps (Console vs Hosted/Dedicated) — backlog + prioritization notes
body:
Context
- We have strong observability in Hosted/Dedicated via Redwood Console + centralized telemetry pipeline.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) has different constraints: customer-managed clusters, limited/no egress, air-gapped installs, customer-owned identity + storage, and strict cardinality/PII constraints.
- This doc lists what we do today in Hosted/Dedicated, what ships (or is feasible) in Private v1 “minimum pack”, and what gaps remain. Goal is to align Console/Tooling backlog with Private Deployments + SRE.

Definitions (rough)
- “Parity” here means: customer + Redwood Support can answer the same operational questions (is it up, is it fast, is it correct, is it getting worse) with similar time-to-diagnosis.
- Not parity: identical UX, identical data retention, or full cross-cluster analytics.

Assumptions / constraints for Private
- No dependency on Redwood SaaS Console for core health (must work fully inside customer environment).
- Default stack is Prometheus + Grafana + log collector (exact collector TBD by min pack decisions; we support export to common sinks).
- Metrics label cardinality must be bounded (no unbounded tenant_id/user_id/request_id labels in Prometheus).
- Logs must be safe-by-default: no request/response bodies, no secrets; prefer hashed identifiers where needed.
- Private customers may want to plug into their SIEM (Splunk/ELK/OpenSearch/Loki/OTLP). We provide documented integrations; we do not run a SIEM.

Current v1 Private minimum pack (what we consider “supported”)
- Grafana dashboards (minimum set): runtime overview, control plane health, GPU/resource pressure, queueing/backpressure, error breakdowns.
- Prometheus recording rules + alert rules mapped to golden signals + key failure modes.
- Structured logs for control plane + runtime with stable field names; baseline log collector config; export examples.
- Installer/Helm wiring + preflight checks + postinstall validation + smoke tests.

What Hosted/Dedicated Console provides today (baseline)
- Unified Console view: per-route/model health, token-level latency/cost, detailed request traces (where enabled), and rollouts + regressions tied to evals.
- Multi-tenant isolation + per-customer drilldowns (internal).
- Cross-region + fleet aggregation with long retention.
- Integrated alert routing/paging policies (internal + some customer configurable).

Gaps table (Hosted/Dedicated vs Private) — with prioritization
Legend
- Feasibility: Now (v1), Near-term (v1.x/v2), Hard (needs new architecture), Not planned.
- Priority: P0 (blocks supportability), P1 (major TTD reduction), P2 (nice-to-have / premium).

1) Token-level cost & latency breakdown in Console
- Hosted/Dedicated: token-level cost/latency panels, breakdown by prompt vs generation tokens, cache hit impact, batch size impact.
- Private today: coarse request latency + throughput; limited token attribution in dashboards.
- Gap: cannot easily answer “why did per-token cost spike?” without manual inference from runtime metrics/logs.
- Constraints: token attribution often requires high-cardinality labels or per-request events.
- Proposal: add low-cardinality histograms + recording rules: tokens_in/out histograms, time_to_first_token, tokens_per_second, cache_hit_ratio. Provide panels + guidance.
- Feasibility: Near-term.
- Priority: P1.

2) Per-route / per-model drilldowns with safe cardinality
- Hosted/Dedicated: drilldown by route, model, customer tier; flexible filtering.
- Private today: dashboards show cluster-wide + namespace-level views; limited route/model dimensions.
- Gap: platform teams want to isolate “route A / model B is slow” without exporting everything.
- Constraints: route/model can explode cardinality if not capped; customers may define many routes.
- Proposal: 
  - Cap route label via allowlist (top N) and aggregate “other”.
  - Provide opt-in detailed mode (documented risk) for smaller installs.
  - Add “route_group” concept in config for observability.
- Feasibility: Near-term (needs runtime + gateway conventions).
- Priority: P1.

3) Request-level tracing (distributed traces)
- Hosted/Dedicated: OpenTelemetry traces with end-to-end spans (gateway → router → runtime), sampling controls, trace search.
- Private today: “where feasible traces” is aspirational; minimum pack is metrics + logs first.
- Gap: hardest incidents (tail lat spikes, partial outages) take longer without traces.
- Constraints: storage + UI (Tempo/Jaeger) + sampling + privacy concerns; air-gapped packaging increases surface.
- Proposal:
  - v1.x: support OTLP export (traces) to customer-managed collector + backend (customer chooses Tempo/Jaeger/etc).
  - Provide span naming + attributes spec (bounded) + sampling defaults.
- Feasibility: Hard for turnkey; Near-term for export-only.
- Priority: P2 for v1 pack, P1 for “premium/private+” later.

4) Console “single pane” inside Private (UI parity)
- Hosted/Dedicated: Redwood Console is the primary UI for ops.
- Private today: Grafana is the UI; no Redwood Console deployed in-cluster.
- Gap: inconsistent UX across deployment modes; SEs have to translate.
- Constraints: shipping Console to Private requires a deployable UI + APIs + auth integration + upgrades.
- Proposal options:
  A) Keep Grafana-first for v1/v2; improve dashboard quality + runbooks.
  B) “Console-lite” (read-only) as an optional helm add-on in Private (future).
- Feasibility: Hard.
- Priority: P2 (nice-to-have, likely premium).

5) Long retention + downsampling
- Hosted/Dedicated: long retention, aggregated views, seasonality.
- Private today: retention defaults likely 7–14d metrics, shorter logs unless customer configures.
- Gap: regressions that emerge over weeks are harder to spot.
- Constraints: customer storage costs; sizing for Prometheus TSDB; operational burden.
- Proposal: provide sizing calculator + recommended recording rules for downsampling; document remote_write to customer long-term store.
- Feasibility: Near-term (docs + values). Turnkey long-term store is Hard.
- Priority: P2.

6) Quality / correctness monitoring tied to evals (regression alerts)
- Hosted/Dedicated: eval harness integration, prompt sets, automatic regression alerts.
- Private today: not shipped; some customers run their own evals.
- Gap: “correctness” regressions (model updates, quantization changes, routing changes) aren’t caught early.
- Constraints: customer data/privacy + compute cost + packaging.
- Proposal: export a minimal “eval hooks” interface:
  - ability to run customer-provided prompt sets against endpoints
  - publish results as Prometheus metrics (low-cardinality) and/or artifacts in customer storage
- Feasibility: Hard (product work). But a minimal “publish eval result metrics” is Near-term.
- Priority: P2.

7) Automated anomaly detection / dynamic baselines
- Hosted/Dedicated: internal analytics + heuristics for anomaly detection.
- Private today: static thresholds in Prometheus alerts.
- Gap: static thresholds are noisy or miss slow burns.
- Constraints: requires historical data + compute + tuning; still must be explainable.
- Proposal: start with SLO burn-rate alerts + better recording rules; consider optional Mimir/Thanos + baseline alerts later.
- Feasibility: Near-term for SLO burn; Hard for true anomaly detection.
- Priority: P1 for SLO burn mapping; P2 for anomaly detection.

8) Built-in incident context: runbook links, “what changed?”, deploy markers
- Hosted/Dedicated: deploy markers + rich annotations; internal runbook links.
- Private today: some alerts include runbook links (in progress); limited deploy/change correlation.
- Gap: oncall spends time correlating upgrades/config changes with metric shifts.
- Constraints: need installer/upgrade controller to emit events; need a canonical annotation channel.
- Proposal:
  - Emit Kubernetes Events + optional Prometheus alertmanager annotations.
  - Add “deployment markers” as Grafana annotations sourced from a small in-cluster endpoint.
- Feasibility: Near-term.
- Priority: P0/P1 (supportability win).

9) Multi-cluster / fleet views (one customer, many clusters)
- Hosted/Dedicated: unified across regions/clusters.
- Private today: per-cluster only unless customer builds federation.
- Gap: larger enterprises want a central view across sites.
- Constraints: federation architecture is customer-specific; network boundaries.
- Proposal: documented reference architecture for Prometheus federation / Thanos / Mimir with Private pack compatibility.
- Feasibility: Near-term (docs only).
- Priority: P2.

10) Secure, support-friendly “bundle for escalation” (one-click diagnostics)
- Hosted/Dedicated: internal tooling collects logs/metrics around incident windows.
- Private today: manual kubectl + export instructions.
- Gap: high friction to get the right data for Support without oversharing.
- Constraints: must avoid exfil of sensitive data; customer approval workflows.
- Proposal:
  - Add “redwood-support-bundle” script (or installer command) that gathers:
    - component versions, helm values (redacted), recent events
    - limited logs (time-bounded, redacted)
    - Prometheus snapshots for key queries (or rules eval outputs)
  - Output a tarball suitable for customer review.
- Feasibility: Near-term.
- Priority: P1.

11) Log search UX and correlation IDs
- Hosted/Dedicated: centralized log search; easy pivot from request to logs.
- Private today: depends on customer sink (Loki/ELK/Splunk); we provide fields and some examples.
- Gap: inconsistent experience; correlation between metrics ↔ logs depends on customer configuration.
- Constraints: we can’t enforce a single backend.
- Proposal:
  - Standardize correlation fields: request_id (if safe), trace_id (if tracing enabled), route, model, pod, node.
  - Provide Grafana dashboard links that pivot to Loki queries when Loki is selected.
- Feasibility: Near-term.
- Priority: P1.

12) RBAC / tenancy views for Private platform teams
- Hosted/Dedicated: Console supports role-based views; internal multi-tenancy.
- Private today: Grafana RBAC varies; many customers use shared Grafana.
- Gap: some customers want per-team dashboards/permissions.
- Constraints: depends on customer IdP; Grafana Enterprise vs OSS differences.
- Proposal: document RBAC patterns; provide namespace scoping; avoid building custom tenancy in v1.
- Feasibility: Near-term (docs). Turnkey is Hard.
- Priority: P2.

13) Capacity planning (GPU pool sizing, headroom, autoscaling recommendations)
- Hosted/Dedicated: internal capacity tooling + recommendations.
- Private today: basic GPU utilization panels; limited “headroom” recommendations.
- Gap: customers ask “how many GPUs do I need for X QPS / tokens/sec?”
- Constraints: workload dependent; we can provide heuristic guidance.
- Proposal: add derived panels: utilization vs queue depth vs p95 latency; add “headroom index” recording rule; link to sizing guidance.
- Feasibility: Near-term.
- Priority: P1.

14) Model lifecycle/rollout observability (canary, fallback, policy routing)
- Hosted/Dedicated: integrated rollout views; policy decisions visible.
- Private today: limited; some routing metrics exist but not first-class.
- Gap: hard to debug “why did router pick fallback model?”
- Constraints: must expose routing decision metrics without high-cardinality; ensure no customer prompt content logged.
- Proposal:
  - Add routing decision counters by decision_reason (bounded enum) + model_variant (bounded)
  - Dashboard panels: fallback rate, policy errors, config reload status
- Feasibility: Near-term.
- Priority: P1.

15) “Correctness” signals for retrieval/reranking/embeddings
- Hosted/Dedicated: richer product-specific panels.
- Private today: focus is on generation runtime.
- Gap: Private customers using embeddings/rerank don’t get tailored dashboards.
- Constraints: need feature parity instrumentation.
- Proposal: expand dashboard catalog by endpoint type (chat/gen/embeddings/rerank) with shared golden signals + specific metrics.
- Feasibility: Near-term (incremental dashboards).
- Priority: P2.

Near-term recommended backlog (next 1–2 iterations)
P0 (supportability blockers)
- Add deploy/upgrade markers + “what changed” annotations (installer emits version/config changes)
- Ensure all alerts include runbook URLs + first-step instructions (oncall feedback)

P1 (high ROI)
- Route/model safe drilldowns (capped cardinality + aggregates)
- Token/throughput/caching recording rules + improved panels
- Support bundle export tool (redacted diagnostics tarball)
- Capacity planning derived panels + linked sizing guidance
- Router fallback decision metrics + panels
- Log correlation standard + Loki pivot links (when Loki enabled)

P2 (future / premium candidates)
- Trace export (OTLP) with span spec + sampling guidance
- Multi-cluster federation reference architecture
- Quality/eval result metric ingestion hooks
- Console-lite in-cluster (optional) — large lift

Open questions / to resolve
- Tracing: do we commit to OTLP export in v1.x, or keep “metrics+logs only” until after GA? (See debate: OTLP exporter support vs Splunk-first.)
- Route/model cardinality: what’s the acceptable cap for “top N routes” in Private defaults? (Need SRE + Telemetry perf input.)
- Correlation identifiers: do we expose request_id by default, and if yes, do we hash it or keep it raw? Security review required.
- Dashboard ownership: Console/Tooling team owns packaging; service owners own metric semantics. Need a clear “panel owner” map.

Notes from recent customer/SE feedback (paraphrased)
- Enterprises want: SIEM export patterns, strict redaction, and proof that dashboards still work after upgrades.
- Platform teams want: a single “is it healthy?” dashboard + clear oncall playbooks.
- Biggest pain is diagnosis of intermittent latency spikes without traces; second biggest is per-route isolation.

Next steps
- Align this backlog with Private minimum pack GA readiness checklist and create concrete tickets for P0/P1 items.
- Review with: Vivek (Product Private), Logan (Telemetry), Rafael (SRE), Bruno (Installer/Helm), Security reviewers (Marcus/Naomi/Kevin) for any new fields/artifacts.
- Target: have P0+top P1 items ready for the first “post-GA” Private pack release (timing TBD by release coordination).
